answer: One robust defense is a stake-and-age reputation system: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits - an ocean of capital for a sparrow-sized gain. The deposit is released only after sustained honest behavior, and proven fraud slashes it. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a marble gaining polish through use, so fresh sybils start with zero trust and cannot outvote established agents. The cost scales linearly with the attack while honest agents pay once.
